citation: NFPA 72, National Fire Alarm and Signaling Code, Chapter 24 (Emergency Communications Systems), intelligibility criteria for Acoustically Distinguishable Spaces: STI ≥ 0.45 (CIS ≥ 0.65) at ≥ 90% of measurement locations; average STI ≥ 0.50 (CIS ≥ 0.70). citation: Analyst construction from commercial pricing guides for acoustic ceiling systems ($5–$15/ft² new-construction installed; designtransitionstudio.com, 2026) and retrofit acoustic panel treatment ($18–$45/ft²; acousticmod.com, 2026). Non-airport benchmarks; the 2–4× ratio at midpoints is directionally supported by these ranges ($10 midpoint vs $31.50 midpoint). Not airport-specific and explicitly described as directional in footnote.

citation: Helsinki-Vantaa (Finavia, silent regime since 2015; gate-area and emergency overrides retained) and Copenhagen Airport, operator-published passenger-communication policies. Amsterdam Schiphol, operator-described "Silent Airport" model with information on FIDS and airport app; 2025 passenger satisfaction 3.84/5, highest in ten years excluding COVID period (Schiphol press release, 2026). No published intelligibility or missed-boarding measurement identified for any of these airports in this research pass.
claim: Helsinki-Vantaa (since 2015) and Copenhagen moved information to screens and apps.[^18] All three are small, single-terminal, point-to-point operations — quieter to begin with. Schiphol is the real comparison: a large intercontinental transfer hub whose reduced-announcement regime rests on FIDS density and a passenger base that expects screens plus app.[^18] None of the four has published measured intelligibility, missed-boarding, or channel-redundancy data.
verification_note: Helsinki 2015 start confirmed via multiple records. Copenhagen policy confirmed via airport website. Schiphol 3.84/5 satisfaction confirmed via Schiphol 2025 annual results press release. 'No published intelligibility data' correctly stated in footnote. Classification of Helsinki/Copenhagen as small/single-terminal is directionally accurate but simplifies complex multi-terminal realities.

citation: San Francisco International Airport, Quiet Airport program outcomes as reported in trade press citing SFO: paging occurrences 492 → 261/day (47% reduction); cumulative paging duration 145 → 58 min/day (60% reduction); gate-seating announcements −40%; onsite noise −40%+; approximately 90 minutes daily announcement reduction. verification_note: All figures confirmed in multiple trade-press records citing SFO. The 492→261 paging-occurrence figures appear in the Airport Industry Review/International Airport Review article; the 90-minute and 40% figures appear in both sources. Methodology remains unpublished. SFO self-report framing used consistently in draft and footnote.

citation: 14 C.F.R. correction: Footnote [^23] revised to add the December 12, 2022 compliance deadline for the 25% accessible kiosk requirement. Original humanized draft cited the rule without specifying when airlines were required to comply.
verification_note: 14 CFR Part 382 is a well-established federal regulation. DOT kiosk rule effective December 12, 2016 confirmed. Compliance deadline of December 12, 2022 (five-year window) confirmed from DOT rule structure.
